raw_response:
*Speaking as the farmer:*

Aiya, another year. I've been working this little patch of 6 mu for over 50 years — same land my father worked. Two sons are in the city now doing construction, so it's mostly me and the old lady handling things. Kids come back to help with the busy seasons, wheat harvest and maize planting.

I do wheat-maize like everyone here. That's just how it is in Quzhou. You plant wheat in October, cut it in June, turn around and plant maize the same week, harvest maize end of September, then start wheat again. No time to waste between.

**For the wheat** (already in the ground since October, now in green-up):
I planted a regular variety, the kind my neighbor 老王 has been using — he gets good yield and the seed shop keeps it. About 15 kg of seed per mu, broadcast and rotavated in. Before planting I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, two bags covers my field nicely. That's always been enough for the base.

Now in spring I'll topdress urea at jointing, maybe 20 kg per mu. If the wheat looks yellow I add a bit more, if it looks dark green I hold back. My eyes tell me. Already watered once after winter, will water again at jointing and once more at flowering if no rain comes. Water from the tube well is expensive now — the electricity meter runs fast — so I don't overdo it.

For weeds I spray the herbicide in spring, everyone does. One pass is enough usually. If I see aphids or rust on the leaves I'll spray once, but most years I don't bother if it's not bad.

I'm hoping for about 450 kg per mu. Last year was 420, year before 460 — weather decides. Combine comes through, I pay per mu, done in an afternoon.

**For the maize** (planting mid-June right after wheat):
No-till planting, the custom operator has a machine that drills through the wheat stubble. Costs some money but saves my back — I can't be ploughing at my age. Hybrid seed, the Zhengdan type or whatever the shop has that year, about 50 yuan per mu.

I put the fertilizer in with the seed — 40 kg of compound per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high, I broadcast another 15 kg of urea. Some younger farmers use that fancy slow-release stuff in one shot, but I stick with what I know.

Rain usually comes in July-August so I often don't irrigate maize at all. If it's dry at tasseling I'll water once, no more than that. Spray herbicide after planting, and if the corn borer is bad I'll spray once. Hoping for maybe 480 kg per mu — last year was a good year, got over 500.

Money is tight but not desperate. Sons send some money home, and the wheat-maize together brings in enough with the subsidy. I don't push for huge yields — just steady, reliable harvests. That's the lesson of 55 years.
